listing.short: Flip cards against the clock in Memory Match, then chase the monster you won around camp. Collect all 20 and top the weekly leaderboard.
listing.long:
Every checkpoint is a timed Memory Match board. Clear it and a monster appears in camp, hopping from spot to spot: you get five chances to catch it before it gets away. Twenty monsters fill your Monster Codex, from Common to Epic.

Your best times go on a weekly leaderboard that resets every Monday at 10:00 UTC, with weekly rewards for players who complete the mission. Right now the camp is running its Halloween Edition.
listing.events: Weekly leaderboard and weekly rewards reset every Monday at 10:00 UTC.

shotlist_tips: Record in the Decentraland desktop Explorer at 1920x1080 or higher; keep the cursor out of frame.
The Memory Match board is screen UI: record it at full screen so the cards and the timer read on a phone.
For the chase, use third person and keep the hopping monster in the middle third of a 16:9 frame so a 9:16 crop keeps it.
Play with sound on: the match, countdown and Halloween stingers carry the clips.
Use Select checkpoint to replay an early level for the chase (12 s per hop) or a late one for panic (3 s per hop).
Keep the two Epic monsters out of public clips: stop before the last checkpoints and close the Codex before the Epic row is visible.

posts.title: Footage: MATCH!
posts.footage: Start a board from checkpoint 1 at full screen. Flip pairs quickly so two or three "MATCH!" popups float up in a row, then clear the board to "Board complete!". First-person screen capture, sound on for the match sound. 6 to 8 seconds. Cut on "Board complete!". Works as a vertical reel if cropped to the board.

posts.title: Footage: the chase
posts.footage: Right after a board, the monster appears in camp. Third person: run at it, miss as it hops away to a new spot, turn, sprint, catch it on the next hop for the sparkle burst. Keep the "Chances" counter visible. 10 to 12 seconds. Cut on the catch burst. Vertical reel: keep the monster in the middle third.

posts.title: Footage: Monster Collected!
posts.footage: Catch a Common or Rare monster, hold on the "Monster Collected!" toast, then open the Monster Codex and show the new monster in its row. 6 to 8 seconds. Cut before the Epic row comes into view; never show an unlocked Epic.

posts.title: Footage: the last 10 seconds
posts.text:
Watch the timer. Not the cards. Wait. Watch the cards.

[FOOTAGE]
posts.footage: Play a later board (use Select checkpoint) and let the timer drop under 10 seconds so it starts blinking red. Make the last match with 1 to 2 seconds left, or let it run out to "Time's up". Full-screen capture, sound on for the countdown. 6 to 10 seconds. Cut on the result.

posts.title: Footage: 30-second trailer
posts.footage: Trailer, 25 to 30 seconds, 16:9 1920x1080, plus a 9:16 vertical cut. 0-3 s: a monster hopping in camp with the player running at it (motion in the first three seconds). 3-10 s: fast Memory Match flips with "MATCH!" popups. 10-18 s: the chase, a miss, then the catch burst. 18-23 s: "Monster Collected!" and the Codex filling. 23-27 s: the weekly leaderboard. 27-30 s: the key art with the link. Captions on screen so it works muted. Keep the Epic monsters out.

posts.title: Behind the scenes: the difficulty curve
posts.text:
How Monster Recon gets harder:

The monster's hop timer starts at 12 seconds and drops 1 second every two levels, down to 3 seconds from level 19 on.

The boards tighten too: 20 seconds on the very first one, 13 on checkpoint 2's first board.

#gamedev #SDK7

posts.title: Behind the scenes: the server keeps score
posts.text:
Leaderboard times and weekly reward claims in Monster Recon don't trust the player's client. They go through an authoritative server that checks the mission before a claim is registered.

The week rolls over Monday 10:00 UTC, and past weeks stay archived.

#gamedev #SDK7
